item.title: Aurangzeb rules out consumption-led growth, says tariff reforms will continue
item.description:
LAHORE: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb has ruled out pursuing liquidity-fuelled, consumption-led economic growth, saying Pakistan must prioritise sustainable, export-led expansion and continue with tariff reforms to improve the competitiveness of its industries.

The finance minister was speaking at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (Lums) on Saturday at an event organised by the American Business Forum (ABF). ABF President Osman Khalid Waheed, former State Bank governor Raza Baqir and Habib Group Vice Chairman Salman Burni also spoke.

Aurangzeb said Pakistan could not afford to repeat the cycle of import-dependent growth that had previously led to balance-of-payments problems and forced the country to seek support from lenders of last resort.

He said the government was committed to continuing tariff reforms, primarily to reduce the cost of raw materials and intermediate goods for exporters, despite concerns over the timing of the measures.

“We are very clear: no matter how much pressure there is, we are not going to go for liquidity-fuelled, consumption-led growth,” he said, adding that Pakistan needed to avoid another cycle in which a temporary acceleration in economic activity was followed by a balance-of-payments crisis.

Aurangzeb said the government had attempted to provide a direction towards export-led growth in the latest budget through measures including the elimination of super taxes, reductions in tax slabs and financing for exporters at 4.5 per cent.

On tariff reforms, he said the government had protected domestic industries for too long without sunset clauses and that the existing approach could not continue indefinitely.

“We are in year two of the tariff reform, and we are going to continue with that; there is no turning back,” he said.

The finance minister also stressed that economic growth needed to generate employment, pointing to the contrast between Pakistan’s growth trajectory and that of its neighbour, where growth of 7 to 8pc, he argued, had not translated into sufficient job creation.

“That’s why you see people there where they are,” he said, emphasising that the sectors driving growth must also address unemployment.

Global outlook remains uncertain

Reflecting on discussions at international forums in New York, London and the annual meetings of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Bangkok, Aurangzeb said the global economy had remained resilient but faced an uncertain and worrying outlook.

He identified growing differences in economic fortunes between oil-exporting and oil-importing countries, as well as economies benefiting from artificial intelligence, as key themes in discussions on global growth.

Energy shocks and the El Nino weather phenomenon had featured prominently in discussions, he said, warning that their effects were intensifying and contributing to food-security concerns in some parts of the world.

He also highlighted high debt levels, limited fiscal space in some economies and the growing importance of digital infrastructure and labour-market preparedness for artificial intelligence.

As trade fragmentation and geopolitical polarisation intensified, regional corridors and regional blocs were emerging as significant opportunities, he said, adding that these developments could be particularly important for Pakistan.

Twin deficits narrow

The finance czar said Pakistan had made significant progress in reducing its fiscal and external imbalances, with the combined twin deficits falling from 12.5pc of gross domestic product (GDP) to 2.6pc by the end of the last fiscal year.

He said the fiscal deficit had dropped to a 22-year low, while the country had recorded primary surpluses for three consecutive years. The current account deficit narrowed to around 0.1pc of GDP, supported by remittances and IT exports.

Aurangzeb said IT export services had risen from less than $1 billion to $4.6bn and were projected to reach $5.5bn in the current fiscal year. Foreign exchange reserves had improved to over three months of import cover, compared with two weeks during the crisis.

Citing three credit-rating upgrades since April last year, he said a recent Panda bond had attracted an order book twice its size, reflecting investor confidence beyond Pakistan’s current IMF programme, due to end in October next year.

Conflict puts pressure on energy security

He further said that Pakistan had managed immediate energy-supply challenges amid the continuing Middle East conflict, with supplies secured through November and arrangements for winter underway.

He said the government had shifted from blanket subsidies to targeted support, citing the high cost of universal subsidies.

Assuming an average household size of four to five people, the programme had reached an estimated 40 million to 50 million people, he said, adding that energy and gas supplies remained areas requiring attention.

Debt management and access to finance

The minister maintained that government borrowing had placed a disproportionate burden on the banking sector, but domestic debt-management operations had helped reduce debt-servicing costs to Rs6.9 trillion against a budgeted Rs8.2tr in the last fiscal year.

He said external debt payments had declined from $26.5 billion last year to $21.5bn in the current fiscal year and were expected to fall further. New external borrowing was largely aimed at replacing existing obligations, rather than increasing the debt burden.

Aurangzeb also highlighted pension reforms, saying new entrants to the civil bureaucracy had shifted from defined-benefit to defined-contribution schemes, while discussions with the armed forces were ongoing.

Population, investment and inclusive growth

The finance minister said the government has identified climate change and population growth as major challenges for Pakistan, urging measures to reduce the country’s 2.55pc population growth rate.

He cited Bangladesh, Indonesia and Iran as examples, saying all three had reduced their population growth rates to below 1pc over a decade. He stressed women’s education, workforce participation and engagement with religious scholars as key measures.

Aurangzeb said restoring investor confidence required macroeconomic stability and the clearance of around $4 billion in outstanding dividend and profit repatriation obligations.

He also highlighted improving domestic investment, citing 11 initial public offerings last year — a 20-year high — and five in the current year.

The finance minister said harmonising federal and provincial regulatory frameworks was essential to attract investment, as businesses often faced differing requirements at both levels. He stressed that reforms in taxation, energy and financing were necessary to sustain growth, improve export competitiveness and create jobs.

France to deploy 70,000 police ahead of new protests
item.description:
FRANCE-CRIME-INVESTIGATIONS-POLICE

France will deploy some 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests this weekend after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, the government said Friday.

President Emmanuel Macron, who according to aides is postponing a visit later this month to Nigeria and Senegal amid the crisis, held a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and was to meet security forces.

He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked the movement that has broadened into a nationwide show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living.

Some 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a press conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city.

Nunez was expected to visit the city Friday to "inspect the security arrangements" at the request of the prime minister's office, it said.

At Macron's meeting with students, "we will present our demands to him -- which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system," Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP.

Macron's government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday.

In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

On Thursday, Macron called for "the utmost severity" against "acts of delinquency", accusing "ultra-left" groups of having sought to "bring down the republic" last weekend.

'Police have a responsibility'

On Saturday, a second round of demonstrations is expected across France.

Lyon's city centre in the southeast will be off-limits to demonstrators this weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares.

Authorities in Marseille had also banned protests but announced Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an "exceptional basis" -- the only one authorised in the southern Bouches-du-Rhone department.

They also reversed a decision to suspend all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.

Some 20 per cent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week.

"In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder," said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons.

The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government's debt pile also troubling investors.

A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 per cent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.

It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 per cent of the vote.

item.title: Apple's foldable iPhone hits stores with $2,000 price tag and scarce supply
item.description:
APPLE-IPHONE/BRITAIN

Apple's first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, hit stores around the world on Friday with a price tag of about $2,000 and less of the fanfare that accompanied previous iPhone launches.

From Singapore and Shanghai to London and Berlin, demand was strong but with sales rationed, there were fewer of the round-the-block queues and overnight camp-outs that once marked new iPhone days.

Competitors such as Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold premium foldable phones for years and the Duo is a test of whether Apple can reinvent the small foldable mobile market the way the iPhone did for smartphones.

It is also an early challenge for Apple's new CEO John Ternus, the former hardware chief who unveiled the phone barely a week after taking charge in September.

Apple's estimated delivery dates for the Duo had slipped to late January within minutes of pre-orders opening a week ago, as demand outpaced supply. The US company called the response "nothing short of extraordinary".

Apple capped pre-orders at two handsets per customer and limited sales to walk-in shoppers. In China, France, Hong Kong, India and Japan they were only available to those who had ordered online.

In Sydney, which was the first Apple store to sell the new passport-shaped phones on Friday, a queue formed outside before opening at 8 a.m. local time (2100 GMT).

"This is a bit of a luxury item for me, because it's so expensive, but I just think, you know what? Life's too short," said Simon Krishnan, a 48-year-old engineer who paid A$3,899 ($2,734) for a 512GB Duo.

In China, a soft consumer market and rising memory costs have led to six straight quarters of declining smartphone shipments, although Apple's market share has rebounded as some buyers trade up to premium devices.

Liu Wei, a 26-year-old healthcare professional, already has a foldable phone from Xiaomi 1810.HK, but still queued outside a Shanghai store from 6 a.m. for Apple's first foldable.

"I've used Apple products for many years and I have more trust (in the brand), so I bought one on launch day to try it out," he said.

Many queued to pick up pre-orders, while others hoped for limited stock or to browse display models.

Others were resellers.

In Hong Kong, May, 38, who declined to give his full name, bought a 256GB iPhone Duo, priced at HK$17,499 ($2,231.73), in an online pre-sale and planned to resell it for a profit of around HK$4,000. "A few meals' worth of money," he joked.

Paul Francis, 53, was one of several dozen fans who queued overnight outside London's Regent Street store in pouring rain.

"Some people think it was mad. Including myself," the charity manager said.

Mixed reviews

Early reviews have praised the Duo's design as well as its sturdy and barely visible hinge, a major feat for phones whose prominent creased screen has long been a drawback and potential deterrent for buyers.

But reviewers said camera compromises, including no telephoto lens, and third-party apps still to be reworked for the new display size could disappoint some buyers.

They also said the folded Duo is less handy for the quick tasks most users do daily and several prominent reviewers recommended against it for many Apple customers.

"It's been a lot of fun trying the Duo out for a week, but it feels like I've gotten to use an extraordinarily polished prototype — not a finished product that I'd want to buy and carry," wrote longtime Apple commentator John Gruber.

Tech commentator Marques Brownlee said in a YouTube review that for a regular person who mostly texts and browses, "it is probably a no. But if the $2,000 doesn't mean much to you, and you like the idea, after the learning curve and getting used to not having facial identification, it is a really fun phone."

In Berlin, YouTube content creator Patrick Wolter was impressed that the Duo works as a phone and an iPad in one.

"I've always found it a hassle to carry around a separate tablet, especially since I already have a laptop and other gear," he said. "In the long run, this will likely end up replacing those other devices."

Tough to find

Apple's entry into the relatively niche foldables market could bring the format to a much broader audience, said Francisco Jeronimo, vice president at market researcher IDC.

IDC expects Apple will take 44 per cent of the foldable market value in 2026 on 31 per cent of units. By 2027, it will become the market leader both in value and units shipped, IDC forecast.

"Apple has made a convincing case for this form factor," Jeronimo said after spending a week with the Duo.

item.title: NCP: Patwary, Hasnat, Sarjis and Asif get promotion; 7 posts abolished
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has published a restructured 195-member committee, promoting Nasiruddin Patwary and Hasnat Abdullah to the position of senior joint convener. Sarjis Alam and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain have also been promoted to senior joint member secretary.

Meanwhile, Samanta Sharmin and Ariful Islam Adeeb, who were senior joint conveners in the previous committee, have been made joint conveners. Abdul Hannan Masud, previously senior joint chief coordinator, has also been appointed joint convener, while Nahida Sarwar Niva, formerly senior joint member secretary, has been made joint member secretary.

The restructured committee was published on the NCP’s verified Facebook page at around 12:15 pm on Friday.

The restructuring has effectively abolished seven posts from the party’s organisational structure. These are chief coordinator, chief organiser for the northern region, chief organiser for the southern region, spokesperson, senior joint chief coordinator, organiser and joint chief coordinator.

However, the restructured committee retains two senior joint conveners and two senior joint member secretaries, as in the previous committee.

In the previous structure, Nasiruddin Patwary held the post of chief coordinator, Sarjis was chief organiser for the northern region, Hasnat was chief organiser for the southern region, Asif was spokesperson and Hannan was senior joint chief coordinator. A total of 42 people served as organisers for the northern and southern regions, while 23 held the post of joint chief coordinator.

The new committee includes 24 joint conveners and six joint member secretaries. While the previous committee had no secretarial posts, the restructured committee has assigned 32 people to 32 secretarial positions, each with one or two assistant secretaries.

In addition, the committee has 19 assistant secretaries, 58 members and 11 organising secretaries.

The NCP began its journey on 28 February 2025 with a 217-member committee. Some additions and removals were made later.

The party’s central committee has now welcomed AK Flora, granddaughter of Sher-e-Bangla AK Fazlul Huq, the first prime minister of undivided Bengal, who joined the party in April, and Ishaq Sarkar, an expelled BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) leader who is also convener of the NCP’s Dhaka South city unit.

Both have been appointed joint conveners. Tarek A Adel, a former adviser to the Jatiya Party, has also been made a joint convener of the NCP’s central committee.

The restructuring has, in effect, elevated Nasiruddin Patwary, Hasnat Abdullah, Sarjis Alam and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain to more influential positions within the party.

Since the party’s formation, these leaders have played significant roles in the last national election and in various recent political issues. Their new positions reflect that influence.

NCP leaders familiar with the process said the leaders’ performance had been taken into consideration during the restructuring.

Three of the NCP’s eight members of parliament (MPs) are among the six top leaders in the restructured committee: convener Nahid Islam, member secretary Akhter Hossen and senior joint convener Hasnat Abdullah.

The party’s other five MPs—Abdullah Al Amin, Atiqur Rahman Mojahid, Abdul Hannan Masud, Mahmuda Alam Mitu and Nusrat Tabassum—have been appointed joint conveners.

The 11 top posts in the previous NCP committee were known as the party leadership’s “Super Eleven”. Following the restructuring, this has become the “Super Six”. The NCP, however, refers to 16 members of its political council as the “Super Sixteen”. The political council is the party’s highest policy-making body.

The 10 members of the political council outside the top six leaders are Abdullah Al Amin, Ariful Islam Adeeb, Atiqur Rahman Mojahid, Abdul Hannan Masud, Ali Ahsan Junayed, Sarwar Tushar, Akram Hossain, Salehuddin Sifat, Mahmuda Alam Mitu and Nusrat Tabassum.

item.title: PHP flaws prompt 12-hour shutdown of digital land services server
item.description:
The Ministry of Land has announced maintenance work to improve the security of its system, following the detection of security vulnerabilities in PHP.

To this end, the ministry has kept the digital land services (land.gov.bd) server shut down for 12 consecutive hours, from midnight tonight (Friday) until noon tomorrow (Saturday).

No land-related services will be available during this period, according to a press release issued by the ministry.

PHP flaws prompt millions of hacking attempts amid rush to patch vulnerabilities

The notice said the security upgrade would be carried out following an urgent cyber alert issued on 22 October by BGD e-GOV CIRT, the government agency responsible for cybersecurity.

Digital land services include mutation, payment of land development tax, collection of land records and mouza maps, land acquisition and requisition, leasing and settlement, land revenue cases, and the land information bank.

The platform also offers a calculator to determine land inheritance, land-related laws and regulations, various forms, and service guidelines.

Bangladesh Bank website shut down to prevent cyberattacks

In the press release, the ministry requested everyone not to make any payments for land services after 11:45pm on Thursday. Apologising for the temporary inconvenience, it sought everyone's cooperation in successfully completing the maintenance work.

Recently, two serious security vulnerabilities were identified in PHP, a widely used programming language for developing and operating websites.

The vulnerabilities have raised concerns about the security of websites operated by various government and commercial organisations around the world.

In response, different organisations have taken initiatives to assess and update the security of their systems.

BGD e-GOV CIRT, the government agency responsible for overseeing cybersecurity-related issues, has also issued an alert about the PHP vulnerabilities.

Bangladesh Bank website shut down to prevent cyberattacks

According to the agency's recommendations, relevant organisations must identify where PHP is being used on their servers.

They must also check whether the versions in use are vulnerable and take necessary security measures.

Earlier, the shutdown of Bangladesh Bank's server in response to the same security vulnerabilities also came to light.

This time, an initiative has been taken to update security by shutting down the digital land services server.

item.title: Dengue cases exceed 45,000 in 19 coastal districts
item.description:
The dengue situation in the country’s coastal belt has taken a serious turn, with reported cases in 19 coastal districts exceeding 45,000 as of October 23 this year, putting growing pressure on upazila hospitals across the Khulna, Barisal and Chittagong regions.
In view of the current trend, experts have stressed the need for more research to understand the disease pattern.
More than 40% of all dengue patients hospitalized in the country this year as of October 23 were admitted to hospitals in the 19 coastal districts. More than 34% of the country’s dengue deaths were also recorded in these districts, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The 19 affected districts are Cox’s Bazar, Bagerhat, Barguna, Barisal, Bhola, Chandpur, Chittagong, Feni, Gopalganj, Jessore, Jhalakathi, Khulna, Lakshmipur, Narail, Noakhali, Pirojpur, Satkhira, Shariatpur and Patuakhali.
According to the DGHS, 1,512 new dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country in the 24 hours leading up to October 23.
As of October 23, a total of 118,502 dengue patients had been admitted across the country. Of them, nearly 44,000 were admitted to government upazila hospitals and private facilities in the 19 coastal districts. During the period, 361 patients died, while 112,111 were discharged from hospitals.
Meanwhile, 206 new patients were admitted in Khulna division, with no deaths recorded in the 24 hours leading up to October 23.
Since January 1, a total of 18,734 dengue patients have been reported in the division, while 17,112 have recovered and returned home.
Researchers, entomologists, physicians and public health experts have pointed to several possible factors behind the spread, including the virus reaching coastal areas with limited previous exposure, water storage due to shortages of safe drinking water, poor drainage and sanitation, and environmental conditions favorable for mosquito breeding.
In 2023, coastal districts accounted for 97,552 of the country’s 321,179 dengue patients, or 30.4%.
Last year, 35,511 patients were hospitalized in the 19 districts out of a national total of 102,358, representing about 34.7%. The 2025 figure covers the entire year, while this year’s data are available only up to mid-October.
Dr Banga Kamal Basu, professor of surgery and a medico-social researcher at Gazi Medical College Hospital in Khulna, said the spread might not be caused solely by mosquitoes, emphasizing the need for further research to understand the pattern.
Stressing the need for more research into dengue, he said the disease pattern might have changed, requiring changes to the system of pathological testing.
Dr Basu, also a public health specialist, called for the establishment of hospitals specializing in the isolation and treatment of epidemic diseases in every district across the country.
Dr Tanmoy Mallick, resident medical officer at Dacope Upazila Health Complex in Khulna, said coastal residents were generally less aware of dengue than urban populations, where the disease had been prevalent for years.
He said relatively heavy rainfall this year had created more breeding opportunities for Aedes mosquitoes in water-filled drains, canals, ponds and other places in rural areas.
People in villages are also frequently outdoors in the early morning and evening, when Aedes mosquitoes are active, increasing their exposure to bites, he said.
Dr Rezaul Karim, health and family planning officer at Koyra Hospital in the coastal upazila, attributed the spread partly to unhygienic surroundings and limited public awareness.
He also identified water scarcity as a major concern in coastal areas. Many residents store rainwater and other available water in containers because of shortages of safe drinking water. Such containers can become breeding grounds for Aedes mosquitoes if left uncovered.
He also pointed to waterlogging in several unions of Koyra, where inadequate drainage allows water to remain stagnant for extended periods.
Karim said awareness campaigns were being conducted to encourage residents to maintain clean surroundings and prevent water from accumulating in household containers, coconut shells and cattle drinking vessels.
Experts have also identified the spread of Aedes albopictus, another dengue-transmitting mosquito species, as a possible factor.
Unlike Aedes aegypti, which is commonly associated with urban environments, Aedes albopictus can breed in vegetation, leaf axils, bamboo joints, coconut shells and other natural or artificial water-holding sites in rural and semi-urban areas.
A survey conducted by the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR) in Barguna in August found Aedes larvae in 26 of 134 water-holding containers examined at homes and other establishments.
The Breteau Index, which measures the number of containers containing Aedes larvae per 100 houses inspected, stood at 53.06. A reading above 20 is generally considered a warning of a high risk of transmission.
The survey identified water shortages, limited access to deep groundwater, household rainwater storage and a lack of awareness about mosquito breeding sites as possible contributors.
The Barguna survey found that around 58% of the Aedes mosquitoes identified were Aedes albopictus, while 42% were Aedes aegypti.
Entomologist Dr Kabirul Bashar, a professor in the Department of Zoology at Jahangirnagar University, said commonly cited estimates of the relative roles of the 2 species in dengue transmission were largely based on findings from other countries.
Their behavior and contribution to transmission in Bangladesh might differ, making further research necessary, he said.
“Perhaps Aedes albopictus has become capable of carrying a higher viral load. This requires detailed research,” he said.
Bashar, also the principal investigator of the Insect Rearing and Experimental Station (IRES), said: “We are beginning research on Aedes mosquitoes.”
Director of Health Services for Khulna division Dr Sheikh Md Mosharraf Hossain said there was no specific program focused on the coastal region, although dengue prevention activities were being carried out nationwide. He also said research was ongoing.
Deputy Director of Khulna Medical College Hospital (KMCH) Dr Sujat Ahmed said Aedes mosquitoes reproduce in stagnant water during and after the rainy season.
The mosquitoes, which previously mainly bit people during the daytime, now appeared to be biting both during the day and at night, he added.
Meanwhile, the government and other agencies have intensified mosquito-control operations, including insecticide spraying in the coastal belt and across the country.
Experts said the rising number of infections and deaths underscored the need for further research into the factors driving transmission in coastal districts, alongside improved drainage, safer water storage, mosquito surveillance and public awareness campaigns tailored to local conditions.

item.title: NCP reshuffles top leadership, retains Nahid Islam as convener
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has reshuffled its top leadership, retaining Nahid Islam as convener and Akhtar Hossain as member secretary.
Nasiruddin Patwary and Hasnat Abdullah have been appointed senior joint conveners, while Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain and Sarjis Alam have been made senior joint member secretaries. Samanta Sharmin has been dropped from the party's highest decision-making body.
The reconstituted committee was announced in a notice signed by Sadia Farzana Dina, the party's office cell secretary, on Friday afternoon.
Nearly 21 months after its formation, the party has reshuffled several key positions despite not holding a national council.
Hasnat Abdullah, who has served as the party's chief organiser for the southern region since its inception, and Nasiruddin Patwary, who previously served as chief coordinator, have been appointed senior joint conveners.
Sarjis Alam, the party's chief organiser for the northern region, and Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, who served as its spokesperson, have been appointed senior joint member secretaries.
Samanta Sharmin, a prominent NCP leader following the July uprising, previously served as senior joint convener. She has now been retained as a joint convener.
Her role in the party reportedly became less active after the NCP formed an electoral alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami for the national parliamentary election held on February 12.

item.title: 35 Bangladeshis repatriated from three European countries
item.description:
Thirty-five Bangladeshis have been repatriated from Europe, including 19 from Italy, 10 from Greece and six from Cyprus.
According to immigration police and airport sources, they arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka on a special chartered flight, PVG 9445, at 8:15am on Friday.
BRAC’s Migration Program provided the returnees with emergency assistance, counselling and financial support to help them reach their respective homes, with assistance from Civil Aviation Security and the Expatriate Welfare Desk at the airport. Representatives from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the European Union were also present.
Shariful Hasan, associate director of Brac, told Dhaka Tribune that Italy, Greece and Germany have been among the European countries from which the organisation has received the highest numbers of returnees in recent years.
He said returnees receive emergency assistance and counselling at the airport, followed by financial support to help them rebuild their lives.
Airport sources said all 35 returnees received assistance under the Prottasha-2 project, jointly funded by the European Union and Brac. They will receive financial assistance after counselling and training.
In 2017, the Bangladesh government signed standard operating procedure (SOP) agreements with European countries to facilitate the repatriation of undocumented or irregular Bangladeshi migrants. Since then, around 5,000 Bangladeshis have returned under the arrangements, with most coming from Cyprus, Italy, Romania and France.

item.title: China orders ‘all-out’ rescue after Tibet quake kills 16
item.description:
China ordered an “all-out” rescue effort in a remote area of Tibet on Friday after an earthquake killed at least 16 people and injured dozens more, state media reported.
Footage showed rescue workers clambering in the dark through some of the 339 houses that Xinhua said collapsed or were damaged in Thursday evening’s 7.0-magnitude quake.
Diners ran out of restaurants and items fell off wobbling supermarket shelves as the tremor struck, footage on state broadcaster CCTV showed.
Xinhua said that 76 people were injured, 11 of them seriously, and that over 12,000 residents were evacuated following the tremor at 10:33pm (1433 GMT).
Hundreds of rescue workers and police were deployed, as well as sniffer dogs and equipment, to locate people under the rubble, CCTV said. More than 300 soldiers were also mobilized.
The epicentre was in Baqing county, a thinly populated area over 4,500 metres (14,800 feet) above sea level and at least a 10-hour drive from regional capital Lhasa, state media said.
One resident told local media that her family had just gone to bed when her home shook, knocking over objects, and that they “rushed outside without even taking the time to get dressed.”
“My legs were shaking the entire time I was heading downstairs, and by the time I reached the bottom, I was so terrified that I burst into tears,” the woman said.
Local residents “are afraid to return to their homes,” she said. “They set up tents along the roadside or spent the night in their cars.”
A man told the Beijing News that the “very strong” quake left his home “creaking and rattling.”
“I was asleep when it hit. Everyone has run outside now and is too afraid to go back in. I’m currently driving to an open area to sleep in my car,” he said.
Broadcaster CCTV also showed emergency personnel with helmets carrying a person and shining flashlights on damaged buildings, some with collapsed roofs.
Tibet is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and Chinese authorities are the only source of official information.
President Xi Jinping said the tremor caused “significant casualties” and took place at a “high-altitude location” in cold weather.
“(We) must go all-out to carry out search and rescue operations and do our utmost to treat the injured, so as to minimize casualties,” Xinhua quoted Xi as saying.
Earthquakes in China are relatively common.
In January 2025, a quake in Tibet’s rural Tingri county killed at least 126 people.
The disaster came little over a year after at least 148 people died in a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China in December 2023, according to state media.
That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people perished in the southwestern province of Yunnan.
A massive tremor in 2008 in Sichuan province left about 90,000 people dead or missing, including thousands of schoolchildren.
On August 26, Tibet was struck by an avalanche of ice and rock and a massive flood, which officially left 43 people dead on the Chinese side and at least 1,400 dead in Nepal.

item.title: PSG v Lyon French Ligue 1 game postponed due to Paris protests
item.description:
Paris Saint-Germain's home Ligue 1 game against Lyon scheduled for this Sunday has been postponed until Monday, the French league announced, following a request by police amid a wave of violent protests in the French capital.
"The LFP takes note of the police decree prohibiting the staging of the game between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais on Sunday at 8:45 pm (1945 GMT)... and has decided to reschedule the match for Monday at 8:30 pm," the French league said in a statement.
Paris police are deploying resources elsewhere as French authorities brace for another weekend of protests in the capital and across the country after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago.
The trouble broke out on the fringe of nationwide protests over the rising cost of living. Since then, authorities have ordered partial curfews in parts of Paris and other cities to prevent further violence.
France's Interior Minister, Laurent Nunez, announced Friday that some 70,000 security personnel will be deployed around the country this weekend as he warned that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media.
Several Paris museums, including the Louvre, have said they will be closed on Saturday, while Art Basel Paris, the biggest annual art fair in the French capital, will shut this weekend, two days early, due to the risk of protests.
The date change for PSG causes a potential headache as the match will now clash with the Ballon d'Or ceremony taking place in London on Monday evening.
Ten PSG players are among the 30 nominees for the most prestigious individual award in football, including last year's winner Ousmane Dembele.
A year ago PSG also had to play a match on the same night as the Ballon d'Or ceremony, after their game in Marseille was postponed by 24 hours due to storms.
While the PSG fixture is affected, the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints taking place on Sunday afternoon at 2:30 pm (1330 GMT) is set to go ahead as planned.
The first ever NFL match to be staged in France will be held at the Stade de France, in Saint-Denis on the northern outskirts of Paris.
The postponement of the PSG game comes after a decision was taken earlier in the week to postpone another French top-flight football game, in the south-western city of Toulouse between the home team and Troyes, from Saturday to Sunday.
Games in France's second-tier Ligue 2 have also been moved this weekend on the request of police.

item.title: The U.S. Treasury wants expanded restrictions on high-tech investments to these ‘countries of concern’
item.description:
The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other “countries of concern.”

The U.S. government has been working for years to deny China and other adversaries investments that could help them boost their military power.

That program began in 2023 when then-President Joe Biden signed an executive order putting restrictions on outbound U.S. investments in sectors such as semiconductors, quantum computing and artificial intelligence going into China. Treasury later established the Outbound Investment Security Program.

In December 2025, Congress passed a law that codified and expanded the program to target more technologies and more foreign countries, including Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Russia.

The inclusion of Russia in the proposed rule has come days after President Donald Trump waived sanctions on Russia following a diesel deal with President Vladimir Putin.

The rule announced Thursday would expand the restrictions to cover investments in hypersonic systems capable of traveling at five times the speed of sound, supercomputing, biotechnology and artificial intelligence, though Treasury used Trump’s favored term for AI, “superintelligence” or SI.

The proposed rule “sends an important signal to markets that Washington is tracking where U.S. capital is flowing and what capabilities it is helping build,” said Craig Singleton, a senior fellow at the think tank Foundation for Defense of Democracies.

The screening of outbound investments “recognizes that capital can accelerate military-relevant capabilities just as surely as technology transfer can,” Singleton said.

Jason Chipman, a former Justice Department lawyer who specializes in cybersecurity, investment rules and export controls as a partner at the law firm WilmerHale, said the new rule “will require more substantial compliance programs to manage risk.”

Treasury’s rule to implement the 2025 law — the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act — would only apply to investments that exceed $50,000 and would exclude many financial investments, including stock purchases.

Treasury will hear public comments on the proposal before issuing a final rule.

“It’s just the first step in a fairly long process to get to changes which presumably will be more enforcement-minded, to put more teeth behind the outbound investment program,” said former U.S. trade official Ryan Majerus, now a partner at King & Spalding law firm.

In Beijing, the Chinese Foreign Ministry said the U.S. should abide by the principles of a market economy and stop interfering in normal economic and trade cooperation between businesses.

Asked about Washington’s proposal to add biotechnology to the list, ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said that “Overstretching the concept of national security, taking discriminatory measures against specific countries, and artificially restricting trade, economic and investment activities serve no one’s interests.”

She added that China will closely monitor relevant developments and take necessary measures to safeguard its interests.

Since Trump’s first term, the United States and China — the world’s two biggest economies — have been locked in an economic and tech rivalry. They’ve restricted the export of sensitive technology and critical products — such as China’s rare earth minerals and America’s advanced computer chips — to each other and slapped tariffs on each other’s products. Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed last year to ease tensions while they engaged in talks, a temporary truce they last month extended into January.

But the sparring continues. In July, the Treasury Department issued a $200,000 fine against a U.S.-based company for failing to report to the department a $92,500 investment in a Chinese artificial intelligence and robotics company by one of its subsidiaries.

—Paul Wiseman and Didi Tang, Associated Press

item.title: American Express layoffs: Thousands of roles slashed in AI push as job losses in financial services pile up
item.description:
It hasn’t been a good week for workers in the banking and financial sector. Yesterday, UK banking giant Barclays announced it was laying off 5% of its workforce, or nearly 5,000 workers, as it transitions more of the bank’s operations to artificial intelligence systems.

Across the Atlantic this morning, an American financial giant made a similar announcement.

The American Express Company (NYSE: AXP), owner of the eponymous credit card and associated financial services, announced that it will slash 5% of its workforce due to AI. Here’s what you need to know.

What’s happened?

On Friday morning, American Express CEO Stephen Squeri announced that the U.S. financial giant was eliminating 5% of its global workforce.

American Express had roughly 76,800 employees at the end of 2025, so a 5% reduction equates to about 3,840 job losses.

Amex confirmed the layoffs to Fast Company when reached for comment.

“We’ve got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over the next few years, we need to become a more agile and efficient organization,” American Express CEO Steve Squeri said on a call this morning with analysts.

Squeri added: “When completed, we believe this exercise will help us operate and execute more effectively and give us greater capacity to invest in our business priorities.”

And yes, artificial intelligence is one of the facets driving the layoffs.

American Express chief financial officer Christophe Le Caillec told CNBC that the restructuring in part would help the company “to prepare for AI.”

“You don’t want to automate processes that are not optimally structured, and so what we’re doing here is to reduce layers and increase spans of controls, so that we can automate and take advantage of AI in the coming quarters and the coming years,” Le Caillec told the network.

American Express stock falls

Following the layoff news, American Express’s stock price fell—but likely not because the company announced layoffs. 

Despite the harm to the individual losing their jobs, Wall Street generally cheers job cuts because they are the fastest way for companies to reduce spending and thus increase their bottom line.

The cuts were announced alongside Amex’s Q3 2026 results today. Those results saw the financial giant report record third-quarter revenue of $20.1 billion, which was up 9% year-over-year. Net income reached $3.7 billion, up from $2.9 billion a year earlier.

Yet the company’s stock price is currently trading down around 3% in early morning trading, likely related to a general fall in markets as Brent crude reaches a six-month high amid the ongoing U.S. conflict with Iran.

Year to date, AXP has now fallen around 13%.

As Fast Company reported yesterday, Barclays—and now American Express—are not the only banking giants that have cut jobs in 2026.

Both Citigroup and HSBC cut 10% of their workforces earlier this year. Standard Chartered said it will cut 15% of its workforce by 2030.

item.title: Europe’s brutally hot summer led to more than 50,000 heat deaths in urban areas alone
item.description:
The summer of 2026 was brutally hot across Europe, with five successive heat waves causing record-high temperatures across the continent. 

Those extremes likely led to more than 50,000 excess deaths in urban areas alone, according to a new estimate.

And some 32,000 of those deaths, or nearly two-thirds of that total, can be directly attributed to climate change, caused by the burning of fossil fuels.

This makes the summer of 2026 likely the “worst on record” for heat-related deaths across much of Europe, according to Clair Barnes, a study author and extreme weather and climate change researcher at Imperial College London.

Dangers of extreme heat

The figures come from two recent studies published in the journal Nature Health.

Researchers from Imperial College London and the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine looked at 854 urban areas across 30 countries (27 of which are in the European Union, plus the UK, Norway and Switzerland). Those areas account for 40% of those countries’ total population. 

By using temperature records combined with climate modeling, they were able to estimate how many excess heat-related deaths occurred every summer between 2000 and 2026. Where governments have released official mortality statistics, these findings align with official figures, the researchers say.

Heat death can be difficult to measure. Heat itself often isn’t listed as a cause of death on death certificates, except in certain instances of heat stroke.

But only counting heat strokes is a “vast underestimation of the actual effect” of extreme heat, says Garyfallos Konstantinoudis, a study author and assistant professor at Imperial College London. 

Heat is one of the deadliest climate change impacts. Extreme heat stresses our cardiovascular and metabolic systems, and can combine with other illnesses to exacerbate health harms. 

This is why this count of excess deaths is an estimate, the researchers note. For the summer of 2026, many countries haven’t yet released their official mortality numbers.

Where they have, though, the researchers’ model estimates align with those figures. The researchers estimated, for example, that May and June heat waves in England and Wales caused more than 2,700 deaths. An analysis by the UK Health Security Agency later identified about 2,880 deaths in that time period. 

The role of climate change

The studies also specifically looked at the role of climate change in these deaths by modeling a pre-industrial world in which human-caused climate change didn’t happen.

Even in that world, temperatures were so dangerously hot that they led to high deaths, Barnes says. 

“But that mortality has been pushed substantially higher by human-caused warming, primarily from the burning of fossil fuels,” she adds. “Across Europe as a whole, around two thirds of those deaths would not have occurred without the additional heat from human activity.” 

Temperatures for that entire summer were 2.9°C above the prior decade’s average. Some days were so hot that they hit 12°C above average. 

The summer of 2026 saw the highest number of urban heat deaths in all 26 years the researchers analyzed. The summer of 2022, which was also marred by multiple dangerous heat waves, was second, with about 29,000 deaths. 

Climate change is warming the entire planet, but Europe is the fastest-warming continent. Over the summer, multiple European governments issued “red weather warnings” about the heat, even closing schools and canceling sports events. 

“These numbers are a stark reminder that our hotter, more extreme summers are having an increasingly severe impact on public health. Behind these statistics are real people whose lives were lost and real families who grieve for them,” Barnes says. 

And they’re also a reminder, she adds, “of the growing need to rapidly transition away from fossil fuels to slow the pace of change and limit future warming.”

item.title: Ukraine war briefing: Russian diesel tankers headed for North America, says Moscow, as US tries to revive peace talks
item.description:
Tankers part of US-Russia deal that could see 500,000 metric tonnes of fuel supplied to world market this month. What we know on day 1,704

Three tankers carrying Russian diesel are on their ⁠way to North America, Russian deputy prime minister Alexander Novak said ⁠on Friday. In ​a statement quoted by Russian news agencies, Novak said the cargoes were ⁠part of a deal that could see Russian companies supply 500,000 metric tonnes to US and world markets in October. “The first ⁠three fuel tankers are already on their ​way to the eastern ‌coast of ‌the Atlantic Ocean, with significant support from the ‌RDIF (Russian Direct Investment Fund),” Novak said. Under a deal announced this month by US president Donald Trump, Russia agreed ‌to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel ​prices in return for Trump temporarily lifting US sanctions on Russian fuel. Reuters reported that the Malta-flagged ⁠medium-sized tanker Agioi Fanendes, loaded with ultra-low sulphur diesel, is expected to arrive in ‌the US on 7 November.

The White House has said that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, where a deepening humanitarian crisis has left thousands of civilians struggling to survive. In a statement on Friday, the White House said both sides had agreed to halt all military operations in the city from 27 October to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and preparations for the evacuation of civilians. Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, which has been under Russian occupation since February 2022, have described increasingly desperate conditions amid severe shortages of food, water and electricity. An estimated 2,000 people remain in the city, with some reportedly forced to survive on weeds, boiled grass, bread and meagre rations. Both Russian and Ukrainian officials said all sides were close to agreeing to a ceasefire.

The Oleshky ceasefire comes as the US is trying to organise new talks aimed at ending the war. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Friday negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US have agreed to technical-level meetings in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi. A US official later said the three ⁠countries may hold their next talks in a couple weeks in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland. Zelenskyy said he hoped a meeting of the countries’ leaders would follow.

The peace efforts follow a rift between Washington and Kyiv in recent weeks and a series of moves by Trump seen as favouring Russia, including limitations being placed on the Starlink communication system that Ukraine uses to protect against incoming attacks. Trump said on Friday that if Ukraine still faced a problem accessing the system, he would straighten it out ​and, if necessary, speak about the matter to SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

As the UK government prepares next week for the first budget under Andy Burnham’s leadership, EU leaders have pressed the new prime minister at a summit in Brussels to contribute more to Ukraine’s defence effort. EU officials say Canada and Japan also should do more to support Ukraine.

The UN nuclear watchdog IAEA said ⁠Fiday ​that repairs to key ⁠power infrastructure near Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia ⁠nuclear power ​plant ‌had been completed ‌under a ‌temporary ceasefire it brokered. The repairs strengthened the plant’s connection ‌to its sole remaining external power ​line, known as Ferosplavna-1, reducing the ⁠risk of another ​loss of ​off-site ​electricity at ​Europe’s largest ‌nuclear ​power ​station.

item.title: As Trump’s time runs out, this could be his most dangerous legacy: a world divided into three | Steve Bloomfield
item.description:
We’ve heard much about the end of the west. At the proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Xi, those fears could crystallise

In the final two years of a US presidency, when Congress has been lost, approval ratings have sunk like a stone and their party has started to think about who’s coming next, the person occupying the Oval Office can feel their power draining away. Domestic legislation, particularly in an era where bipartisan cooperation is almost nonexistent, grinds to a halt. But as the days tick by until the end, and as presidents begin to think about their legacy, there is one part of the job where they still have power: the rest of the world.

In the final weeks of his presidency in 1992 George HW Bush sent 28,000 American troops to Somalia to help end a famine. For Bill Clinton, it was a quixotic attempt to bring peace to the Middle East by ending the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Barack Obama restored diplomatic ties with Cuba, making a historic visit to Havana, as well as a final, successful push on the Iran nuclear deal.

item.title: PCB releases Sufiyan Moqim from tri-series squad, adds Maaz Sadaqat as cover
item.description:
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Sunday released left-arm wrist spinner Sufiyan Moqim from the national men’s squad for the ongoing One-day International tri-series involving England and Sri Lanka, citing the nature of the pitches in Lahore, while adding left-handed batter Maaz Sadaqat as cover for players carrying minor niggles.

In a brief statement, the PCB said Sufiyan had been released from the squad “keeping in view the nature of Lahore pitches” and would return to domestic cricket. Maaz, meanwhile, had been added as cover for players with minor niggles.

The move comes as the tri-series shifts to the Gaddafi Stadium after the opening three matches in Rawalpindi. Pakistan have won both their league games so far, beating Sri Lanka by 37 runs and England by 87, and face England again in Lahore on Sunday. The pitches in Rawalpindi generally favoured pace, limiting opportunities for specialist spinners.

Sufiyan, who hails from Azad Kashmir, has represented Pakistan in limited-overs cricket since making his T20I debut in 2023. He is best known for his record-equalling figures of five for three against Zimbabwe in a T20 International and was named Player of the Tournament in the 2026 Pakistan Super League while playing for Peshawar Zalmi. In ODIs, he has taken eight wickets in four matches.

Maaz, 21, has attracted attention with his aggressive batting. The Peshawar-born left-hander made an immediate impact on his ODI debut against Bangladesh earlier this year and recently impressed in the T20I series against Sri Lanka, scoring consecutive half-centuries, including a blistering 96 off 51 balls that helped Pakistan post their highest T20I total at home.

An occasional left-arm orthodox spinner, Maaz had initially been left out of the tri-series squad.

The updated squad, led by Shaheen Shah Afridi, now includes Maaz as Pakistan continue their campaign in Lahore ahead of the final on Oct 31 at the same venue.

JS body calls for silk mechanization, easier raw material access
item.description:
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Textiles and Jute on Saturday recommended mechanizing operations under the Bangladesh Sericulture Development Board and ensuring easier access to yarn, dyes and raw materials for marginal weavers.
The committee made the recommendations at its first meeting of the 13th National Parliament at the National Parliamnet with its Chairman Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia, MP, in the chair.
The committee also recommended ensuring transparency, integrity and accountability in the tender process by avoiding repeated awards of tenders to the same institution and providing opportunities to other eligible institutions.
It suggested involving local members of parliament in taking necessary steps to make yarn, dyes and other raw materials more accessible to marginal weavers through weavers' associations or the appointment of dealers, said a press release of parliament secretariat.
The committee further recommended examining the operations of the Bangladesh Handloom Board's office at Ranir Bandar in Dinajpur and verifying whether the land associated with the office had been leased out or allocated through other means before taking necessary action.
At the meeting, the committee reviewed the activities of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute and its subordinate departments and agencies. Officials presented an overview of their operations and briefed the committee on the ministry's initiatives under the government's 180-day program and the progress of ongoing projects.
The committee also recommended conducting all activities of the Ministry of Textiles and Jute in line with the prime minister's election manifesto and taking appropriate and necessary initiatives to implement its commitments.
At the beginning of the meeting, the chairman paid tribute to Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman, former BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia and the martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the Great War of Liberation. He prayed for the salvation of their souls.
He also paid tribute to those killed during the July 2024 movement and expressed deep sympathy for those injured in the movement.
Textiles and Jute Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, MP, State Minister Md Shariful Alam, MP, and committee members S M Faisal, MP, Md Abdullah MP, Rezeka Sultana, MP, Md Afjal Hossain MP, Hafez Muhammad Rabiul Bashar, MP, and Mahabuba Hakim, MP, attended the meeting.
The ministry secretary, heads of relevant departments and agencies, concerned officials and officials of the Bangladesh Parliament Secretariat were also present.

item.title: Health Minister: Community clinics to be renamed family welfare centres
item.description:
Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Saturday announced that all community clinics across the country will be renamed family welfare centres as part of plans to expand healthcare services at union level.
He made the announcement while outlining the government’s plans to improve healthcare infrastructure and services during surprise visits to several health facilities in Mymensingh.
Earlier in the day, the minister visited Fulbaria and Tarakanda Upazila Health Complexes before inspecting Mymensingh Medical College Hospital, where he expressed dissatisfaction over various irregularities, including medical equipment found in a garbage dump and doctors and nurses failing to report to work on time.
During his visit to the hospital around noon, he inspected the labour ward, measles isolation ward and dengue ward. He also examined the quality of treatment, the ward environment and the condition of washrooms.
The minister expressed anger after finding rubbish on the ground floor of the hospital's new building. He also ordered a swift investigation and the submission of a report into the discovery of used cannulas, syringes and other medical equipment in the hospital's garbage dump.
He said action would be taken against those found negligent in their duties, including staff who failed to arrive at the hospital on time. The minister also questioned why a patient in the gynaecology ward had to purchase saline from outside and instructed the hospital authorities to take necessary measures.
He further sought an explanation for the delay in submitting an investigation report into a fire at the hospital more than a month ago. The authorities told him that the report has been delayed due to holidays.
Earlier, during his visits to Fulbaria and Tarakanda Upazila Health Complexes, he said the government planned to upgrade both health complexes to 151-bed facilities.
A large-scale tendering process worth around Tk 16,000 crore for the health sector would be launched within the next 15 to 20 days, he said, adding that steps would be taken to ensure the supply of necessary medicines to the community clinics after they are renamed family welfare centres.
